description: Customer-service platform with Support ticketing for tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.
self_serve_details: Zendesk lists self-serve trials and paid Support/Suite plans. API requests require a verified user; OAuth access is instance-bound, while public multi-customer integrations must use a global OAuth client. The opened pricing page does not map API access to a specific trial or plan, so a free-credential conclusion is not assigned.
api_details: The official Support/Ticketing API covers tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows with standard REST resources. Rate limits and certain advanced entitlements are account/endpoint dependent; this assessment does not infer MCP from the REST API.
mcp_details: No first-party Zendesk MCP server was established in the reviewed material. This is an unresolved field, not a NOT_FOUND claim.
blocker: Verified account access and OAuth client setup are required; public distribution requires global OAuth. Plan-to-API entitlement and official MCP availability remain unresolved.
buildability_rationale: A broad official REST API supports core support actions, but the required verified-user/OAuth setup and global OAuth rule for multi-customer distribution add material constraints.

description: Customer-service platform for support conversations, messaging, shared inboxes, tickets, and customer data, with Fin AI features.
self_serve_details: Intercom offers self-serve trial signup, but the official Conversations API reference says the API is available only to apps with a trial or active subscription. Plan, usage, and API scope conditions still apply; the pricing page does not state trial duration in the opened text.
api_details: Directly reviewed REST documentation covers conversation creation, listing, replying, and management; the first-party MCP guide additionally documents access to conversations, contacts, companies, articles, and other API-backed tools. The REST endpoint inventory was not exhaustively sampled in this batch, so breadth is conservatively MODERATE.
mcp_details: Intercom hosts official remote MCP endpoints: https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp for US and https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp for EU workspaces. Official docs list 14 tools; user permissions and requested OAuth/API permissions govern access. AU-hosted workspaces are not yet supported.
blocker: A workspace trial or active subscription is needed for the Conversations API; public apps use OAuth, and MCP is unavailable for AU-hosted workspaces.
buildability_rationale: Documented REST operations and an official MCP provide useful agent access, but subscription, OAuth consent/scope, and workspace-region requirements affect rollout.

description: Customer-support helpdesk for ticketing, shared inboxes, customer portals, knowledge bases, and agent workflows.
self_serve_details: The current Freshdesk support plan matrix marks API-key functionality unavailable on Free and available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise. Pricing offers self-serve trial entry for paid plans, but trial entitlements were not tested. Freshdesk MCP is generally available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise with plan-based action allowances and optional action packs.
api_details: The official REST v2 reference documents ticket CRUD, conversations/replies, contacts, companies, agents, ticket fields/forms, and other helpdesk resources. API quotas are plan-based. The separate official MCP surface is an API-key-authenticated agent interface, not a separate REST API type.
mcp_details: Freshworks' first-party Freshdesk MCP endpoint is https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp. Freshdesk support says GA began September 10, 2026, supports MCP-compatible clients, and currently authenticates with an API key only. Growth, Pro, and Enterprise have annual included action allowances and per-minute limits.
blocker: Free excludes API access; verified API-key/role access, paid-tier rate limits, and the Freshdesk MCP action allowance/add-on structure constrain deployment.
buildability_rationale: Freshdesk offers broad REST resources and a first-party MCP integration, but a supported paid plan, verified agent credentials, and usage quotas are material requirements.

description: Customer-operations platform with a shared inbox and APIs for syncing, retrieving, creating, updating, and deleting conversations and related resources.
self_serve_details: Front provides a free developer environment for API work, limited to three teammates. API tokens are a quick path for an internal/single-customer integration; public integrations must use OAuth unless Front grants an exception. Public partnership/listing is a separate process.
api_details: The Core API supports CRUD across contacts, comments, tags, conversations and other entities; webhooks support real-time events. Front also documents separate Channel API, Plugin SDK, and connector surfaces, which are not counted as Core REST endpoints here.
mcp_details: Front operates an official open-beta remote MCP server at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp. It uses OAuth 2.1/PKCE-compatible confidential client credentials, per-user authorization, and read/write/send scopes; clients requiring DCR cannot connect.
blocker: Public integrations require OAuth; Front MCP is open beta and requires a client ID/secret (no DCR). Tools inherit the user's role and scopes.
buildability_rationale: A free developer environment and broad REST/webhook surfaces enable development, but public distribution, beta MCP compatibility, OAuth setup, and user-scoped authorization are material constraints.

description: B2B customer-support platform with programmatic access to customer accounts, issues, contacts, messages, and related support data.
self_serve_details: Official API and support docs establish API/MCP credentials inside an existing Pylon workspace, but the reviewed pricing URL repeatedly redirected to a demo-booking page. A public signup/trial path and the precise plan entitlement for API/MCP therefore remain unresolved.
api_details: Pylon's first-party API/Webhooks material says integrations can read and act on data across accounts, contacts, issues, messages, tasks/projects, knowledge base, custom fields/objects, tags, macros, surveys, teams, and users; webhooks push events to customer endpoints.
mcp_details: Pylon's official MCP endpoint is https://mcp.usepylon.com/. It uses browser OAuth only, acts on behalf of the logged-in user, and supports issue/account/contact access; notebook block content is not currently retrievable through MCP.
blocker: REST tokens require a Pylon Admin; MCP requires a Member/Admin OAuth login and cannot use machine credentials. Account/trial/plan entitlement remains unknown.
buildability_rationale: A broad documented REST/webhook surface and official hosted MCP make the connector technically feasible, but credentials are role-gated, MCP is OAuth-only, and pricing/account access was not established.

description: Helpdesk and customer-support suite with ticketing, live chat, knowledge base, automation, and call-center features.
self_serve_details: LiveAgent advertises a 30-day no-credit-card trial and paid per-agent tiers. Its hosted MCP tools count against the account's AI-credit budget; the current API v3 reference is available from within a customer account, so the trial does not by itself prove every API operation or entitlement.
api_details: The opened public REST API v1 reference documents conversations/messages, customers, companies, knowledge-base articles, reports, tags, files, and agents. LiveAgent also says API v3 documentation and interactive testing are available inside the account; v3 endpoint details were not inspected here.
mcp_details: LiveAgent offers a tenant-specific hosted MCP server at https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp with Streamable HTTP and either generated Bearer tokens or OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + PKCE. Tools execute as the agent and are limited by their role; MCP calls count against AI credits.
blocker: The server URL is tenant-specific, agent role permissions apply, MCP uses AI credits, and the current v3 API reference is account-gated.
buildability_rationale: A broad REST surface and first-party MCP are documented, but tenant-specific setup, role-scoped actions, credit consumption, and limited public visibility into current API v3 details affect implementation.

description: Support platform for customer-service teams with thread, customer, tenant, and workflow data exposed through GraphQL and agent tooling.
self_serve_details: Plain advertises a seven-day free trial with no credit card and self-serve Foundation pricing. API credentials require a workspace machine user and explicitly selected permissions; the opened pricing table does not reliably map every API/MCP capability to each tier.
api_details: Plain's GraphQL API is the same API used by the product and its documentation says it has no UI/API capability gap. The docs provide customer/thread operations and a schema/typed SDK; breadth is judged broad for the documented support data model, not by endpoint count.
mcp_details: Plain operates https://mcp.plain.com/mcp with OAuth. The official guide lists 30 read/write tools spanning threads, customers, tenants, and support actions; OAuth inherits the user's access and requires openid offline_access scopes.
blocker: A workspace and machine-user permission setup are required for API keys; hosted MCP requires interactive OAuth and client support for token refresh/scopes. Plan mapping is incomplete.
buildability_rationale: Plain offers a broad documented GraphQL API and first-party MCP, but credentials are scoped, OAuth is user-bound, and ongoing plan/API entitlement details need confirmation for a production deployment.

description: Customer-support platform with a shared inbox, conversations, customer records, knowledge bases, workflows, and reporting.
self_serve_details: Help Scout's API and MCP access is included on Standard, Plus, and Pro plans; the official pricing page also lists a separate Free plan. The MCP guide says new connections are read-only; Reports require Plus/Pro and Docs knowledge-base tools need a separate Docs API key.
api_details: Help Scout documents Inbox API v2 and Docs API surfaces. The Inbox API is HTTPS/JSON and covers conversations, customers, users/inboxes and reports; the official MCP guide lists those resources plus optional Docs content. No endpoint count is inferred.
mcp_details: Help Scout's official remote MCP endpoint is https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp. New connections are read-only and access follows the connecting user's Help Scout permissions; Standard/Plus/Pro include API access, reports need Plus/Pro, and Docs search needs a separate Docs API key.
blocker: Paid Standard/Plus/Pro entitlement and an active invited user are required; MCP is read-only, reports need Plus/Pro, and Docs has a separate API key.
buildability_rationale: A documented REST API and official MCP support core retrieval use cases, but paid-plan/API access, account permissions, read-only MCP, and separate Docs credentials constrain actions.

description: Customer-support helpdesk for ecommerce teams, with ticketing and an AI Agent available alongside the support inbox.
self_serve_details: Gorgias offers self-serve trial signup and paid helpdesk plans. Its API credentials are available on Helpdesk plans to owners/admins; the official first-party MCP is included at no extra cost for paid plan customers and remains open beta in the reviewed announcement.
api_details: Gorgias has an official REST/JSON API reference and first-party help documentation says the API reads and writes helpdesk data. The API surface is relevant for core support integration; this batch did not exhaustively enumerate individual endpoint groups, so breadth is conservatively MODERATE.
mcp_details: Gorgias' first-party remote MCP endpoint is https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp?gorgias_subdomain=YOUR-SUBDOMAIN. It uses OAuth and is in open beta for paid helpdesk customers; the company says it can search tickets/customer history, analyze support data, inspect macros/rules/tags, and draft AI Agent guidance.
blocker: API keys require owner/admin access and grant full account data; public apps require OAuth2; the official MCP is paid-plan-only and open beta.
buildability_rationale: Gorgias has documented REST credentials and a first-party MCP, but account role, broad token scope, public OAuth onboarding, paid subscription, and beta status are material constraints.

description: Customer-service platform with a REST API for customer profiles, conversations, messages, tasks, answers, reports, and related support workflows.
self_serve_details: Gladly's official company blog labels its product pricing as Custom (sales-led), while the homepage offers Get a Demo/Try it yourself; neither establishes an API-specific commercial entitlement. For an existing instance, an administrator must grant API User permission before an agent can create/use a token. Sandbox access requires purchasing/contacting a CSM or support team.
api_details: The official REST reference enumerates customers, conversations/items, agents, answers, tasks, reports, teams, communications, exports, topics, and webhooks. It also describes a sandbox endpoint, with sandbox provisioning requiring purchase/contact with a CSM/support team.
mcp_details: No first-party Gladly MCP offer was established. The official developer API index and setup guide were opened and targeted official-domain MCP searches were run, but no complete source repository/catalog audit was performed; status remains UNKNOWN.
blocker: Requires an existing Gladly tenant and administrator-granted API User permission; sandbox testing is separately purchased/contact-mediated. MCP availability is unknown.
buildability_rationale: The broad REST/webhook API is usable for authorized customer instances, but role-gated token creation and tenant/sandbox access constrain a general-purpose build; no MCP capability is claimed.
